_comment: The Table View's OTHER rendering of Last Talk Time, captured during the
Milestone 5D-1 discovery pass on 2026-08-03.
WHAT THIS FIXTURE IS, EXACTLY. It is the sibling capture in this directory
— a real extraction from the live dashboard — with ONE cell replaced: the
Last Talk Time cell now holds `1785745430123`, which is a real value read
off the live Table View in the same pass (row TK-51105-04HY-122432). Two
real observations, combined so one fixture exercises one parser. Nothing
here is invented, and the substitution is stated rather than implied.
WHY IT MATTERS. Reading all 320 rows in a single pass found Last Talk Time
rendered TWO ways: 200 rows carried a bare epoch like the one below, and
120 carried the formatted `03-Aug-2026 13:53` the sibling fixture holds.
The split fell exactly on the pager boundary — the page read first was raw,
the page read last was formatted — because this React table formats its
timestamps client-side after the row renders. The same vehicle was observed
unparseable on a cold read and parseable on a warm one.
Before Milestone 5D-2 a row like this produced `available: false` with `in
a format this system does not recognise`: a true statement about the parser
and a false impression about the portal, which had reported the time
perfectly well. Roughly three fifths of reads were affected.
1785745430123 is 2026-08-03T08:23:50.123Z. Note what the epoch form does
NOT need: renderOffsetMinutes is still captured below and is still -330,
but the normalizer must not apply it to this value — an epoch already
carries its own zone, and the payload records that by reporting
basis `epoch_milliseconds` with a null offset.
